title: action/v1
description: The agent's decision for one turn (IC-3): a signed target-position vector plus optional execution tolerance, rationale, and telemetry. This is the WIRE form, tuned for LLM ergonomics: target leverage values are decimal STRINGS (or bare JSON integers), never fractional JSON numbers - a JSON number with a fractional part is rejected with reason float_target, so no float ever enters a money path (DET-2/DET-4). The engine canonicalizes to integer lev_1e4 in ActionParsed; only that canonical form is hashed. Leverage-cap/turnover/kill-switch limits are deliberately NOT validated here: a well-formed over-limit action parses successfully and is then blocked by a recorded RiskCheck gate, preserving attempted-vs-executed evidence (SAFE-1).

schema.description: Schema name and major version of this document.

intent_kind.description: Optional intent discriminator (the IC-3 extensibility seam, applied at the M0 audit). Absence means 'leverage_target' - every v1 trading action is a leverage-target intent, and `target` is conditionally required exactly when intent_kind is 'leverage_target' or absent (the allOf/if/then above; vacuous truth of the if-schema when the member is absent makes absence equivalent to the const). This enum is on the additive-tolerant list (VERSIONING.md): a future non-trading intent kind (e.g. a commerce 'purchase_intent' carrying an AP2-style cart) arrives as a new enum member with its own conditionally-required payload branch - a MINOR bump, not an action/v2 major. The engine canonicalizes the discriminator into the hashed parsed form (ActionParsed.intent_kind, constant 'leverage_target' for every trading action), so determinism is unaffected.

target.description: Map: market alias (as shown in the observation, e.g. 'BTC') -> signed target leverage on NAV. Sign = direction (negative = short), '0' = flat, magnitude = leverage multiple. Example: {"BTC": "-1.5"} = short 1.5x NAV. This is the entire action space: target positions, not raw orders.

additionalProperties.description: Target leverage: a decimal string with at most 4 fractional digits (e.g. "1.5", "-0.25", "0") or a bare JSON integer. Parsed EXACTLY (decimal re-parse of the raw text, never via binary float) to an integer in 1e-4 leverage units ("1.5" -> 15000). Fractional JSON numbers are schema-invalid by construction.

anyOf.description: Signed decimal string, <= 4 fractional digits, no exponent; NaN/Infinity are unrepresentable by the grammar.
Whole-number leverage as a JSON integer (integers are exact; only fractional JSON numbers are banned).

max_slippage_bps.description: Optional. Maximum acceptable modeled slippage versus the next-bar-open reference price, in integer basis points (agent-facing bps for ergonomics; stored engine-side as slippage_1e8, 1 bp = 10000 in 1e-8 units - exact conversion). Orders whose modeled slippage exceeds this are cancelled with reason max_slippage_exceeded.

comment.description: Optional free-text rationale. Never interpreted by the engine. It is NOT copied into the canonical parsed action: the verbatim response bytes (which contain it) are content-addressed into raw/, keeping rationale redactable under the share profile without touching chained records.

usage.description: Optional self-reported token usage; copied by the harness into AgentResponded.token_usage. Advisory telemetry, never validated, excluded from the canonical parsed action (it is telemetry, not intent).

input_tokens.description: Agent-reported input/prompt tokens consumed for this decision.

output_tokens.description: Agent-reported output/completion tokens produced for this decision.

ext.description: Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md): engine-ignored, recorded verbatim in raw/ only (not in canonical parsed form). Keys SHOULD be reverse-DNS or x_-prefixed; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value).

ext_value.description: JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap.

anyOf.description: JSON string (decimal values ride as strings, e.g. '0.7').
Integer within the I-JSON exact range (JCS round-trips it byte-identically).
Object whose values are all JCS-safe.
